title: Niche topics (2): in-specie, DDPI, nomination and cash flows
objectives: Describe DDPI / POA scope and corporate actions.
Ask about high-water-mark resets and top-up rules.
body_md:
| Topic | What to explain | Investor takeaway |
|---|---|---|
| In-specie transfer | Many providers accept existing shares instead of cash, and can return securities instead of selling on exit (check the provider's policy). | You may be able to fund a PMS with shares you own. |
| DDPI / POA scope | The authority signed over the demat and bank account defines what the manager can do. | Read what you authorise before signing. |
| Nomination & corporate actions | Nominee, dividends, bonuses and voting rights all sit in the client's own demat. | Add a nominee to your PMS demat too. |
| High-water mark resets | Check whether and when the high-water mark resets, and whether fees are charged on contributions or withdrawals. | Ask how the profit share is calculated after a loss. |
| Top-ups and withdrawals | Rules on minimum top-ups and partial withdrawals vary by provider and agreement. | Know the rules before you need the money. |

Regulatory figures here should be checked against current SEBI and APMI rules before each training cycle.
example: A client holds ₹55 lakh of blue-chip shares. Many providers accept shares in kind (in-specie), but selling them to fund the PMS can trigger tax, so you check the provider's policy and the tax first.
say: Add a nominee to your PMS demat account too.
Read what you authorise before signing the DDPI.
never: The authority is just a formality.

check.q: A client wants to fund a PMS with shares they already own. What is true?
o: It is never allowed; only cash is accepted
Many providers accept an in-specie transfer; check the provider's policy
The shares must be sold first by the distributor
Only mutual fund units can be transferred
check.why: Many providers can also return securities instead of selling on exit.

check.q: What does the DDPI / POA scope define?
o: What the manager can do in the client's demat and bank accounts
check.why: The authority signed over the demat and bank account defines what the manager can do.

check.q: Where do dividends, bonuses and voting rights sit in a PMS?
o: In the client's own demat account
check.why: Because securities are in the client's demat, corporate actions and voting rights sit there.
